source_executable.origin: GitHub Actions artifact 11373183170 from Korean Localization Test Build run 37379204466

proof: EXE VA 0x4DDBE5-0x4DDC02 copies four dwords (16 bytes) from the Edit License text buffer to 0x7C23E0..0x7C23EF on player-name commit.
EXE VA 0x4DD855-0x4DD872 copies exactly 0x10 bytes from 0x7C23E0 into the Edit License backup/input state.
EXE VA 0x4DDB4C-0x4DDB59 calls the name-entry bound setter with min=1 and max=0x10; append logic at 0x4692BB-0x4692E3 only appends while length < max-1.

native_input_encoding.selector_to_byte: EXE VA 0x468D40 indexes byte table at 0x64C81B + page*0x25 + selection
native_input_encoding.symbol_page: page 2 contains punctuation plus game-specific high-byte glyph codes
native_input_encoding.append: EXE VA 0x4692CE-0x4692E3 writes exactly one selected byte per accepted character

edit_license_render_use.display_source: 0x7C23E0 is passed directly as a string source at EXE VA 0x4DE48A to Edit License text-object setup
edit_license_render_use.implication: Raw UTF-8 Hangul in this field would be seen as legacy bytes by stock name rendering unless localization hooks cover the relevant consumers.

player_save_base_surface.note: These references include uses of 0x7C23E0 as the player-save structure base, not 145 proven name renderers. Their breadth is sufficient to require consumer classification before changing name encoding.

decision.why_hold: Exact storage and native byte encoding are now proven, but Hangul cannot be represented natively by the stock one-byte selector. Changing storage without first covering downstream name rendering and replay/ranking/network/save compatibility would be unsafe.
decision.next_safe_work: Map/classify direct player-name consumers, then choose a compatible Korean storage/transport policy before changing 66743AA8 or runtime behavior.
